claims.text: High configurational entropy and severe local lattice distortion synergistically govern the intrinsic thermal stability and resistance to atomic diffusion of nearly equiatomic five-transition-metal HENA.
High configurational entropy and lattice distortion suppress grain growth.
High configurational entropy and lattice distortion suppress nanoprecipitate formation.
There is a critical temperature above which mixing entropy can no longer overcome phase-separation or coarsening forces.
A five-component ratio of 50:20:20:20:20 is nearly equiatomic.
Fast cooling or high-energy milling ensures a single-phase solid solution with high configurational entropy and significant local lattice distortion.
Restricting particle size to below 50 nm maximizes surface-to-volume-ratio effects.
Sluggish diffusion and local lattice-distortion fields impede atomic mobility and grain-boundary migration.
Impeded atomic mobility and grain-boundary migration kinetically trap a single-phase structure.
High mixing entropy lowers the Gibbs free energy of the solid solution.
Severe lattice distortion creates high energy barriers for atomic diffusion and produces sluggish diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion retards grain growth.
Sluggish diffusion prevents the nucleation of secondary phases or nanoprecipitates.
The HENA will have significantly slower grain-growth rates than traditional binary or ternary alloys under comparable thermal exposure.
The HENA will show a delayed onset of phase decomposition relative to traditional binary or ternary alloys.
The HENA will retain a single-phase structure and high hardness for extended periods at temperatures where traditional alloys coarsen or decompose.
Above a critical temperature, entropy stabilization will fail and rapid grain growth and phase separation will occur.
Binary, ternary, and lower-entropy control alloys will undergo grain growth and phase separation at lower temperatures because they have less configurational entropy and lattice distortion.
Below a critical nanoparticle size, surface energy dominates bulk entropy effects and invalidates the intrinsic-stability model.
Significant departure from equiatomic composition reduces configurational entropy below the threshold needed for solid-solution stability.

contradictions.description: The ratio 50:20:20:20:20 is described as nearly equiatomic, but it sums to 130 rather than 100 and assigns one component a much larger fraction than the other four.

The main hypothesis presents thermal stability and diffusion resistance as intrinsic consequences of the high-entropy state, while the uncertainty field explicitly states that sluggish diffusion may instead be a synthesis-dependent kinetic artifact.
